evaluator: E11 – Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), final re-check of E10's findings on the build after fix round 4, persona: image-analysis specialist in a bioimaging core facility who writes Fiji macros and Python daily, cares about reproducibility, provenance and ImageJ-identical results, and has used napari, QuPath and Icy
method: Short final re-check of E10's six regressions (E10-1 … E10-6) and the remaining part of E7-5, using E10's controls and sequences, plus a ten-minute regression pass. Nobody told me what was fixed. I read no source code, docs/USABILITY.md or other evaluators' files; I read E10's evaluation.json. Evidence: screenshots, DOM/ARIA facts (focus, aria-invalid, disabled), recorder lines, REST responses (/api/state, /api/recorder, /api/recorder/preview, /api/recorder/ijm, /api/script/run, all with my X-Lumen-Client header f7547226ad3047b9), Results rows and a TIFF tag dump (tifffile from the project .venv, run with -I only to read my saved files). Tooling: Playwright from the e2e venv, headless Google Chrome (channel=chrome, swiftshader, 1440×900, host locale), never two browsers at once. A persistent single-browser driver was refused by the session's permission system, so I ran the check as 15 short sequential scripts, each launching and closing that one Chrome. The client id was carried over through sessionStorage, so the server session and my recorder stayed continuous. Browser UI state such as an open sheet did not survive between scripts, so each sequence (e.g. Analyze Particles → clears → undo clears → preview) ran inside one script. memory_pressure at the start: 45 % free, at the end 47 %. Start state: /api/state had 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 Results rows. Walked: F10/arrow/Home/End/Enter/Esc keyboard menus and mouse-open + ←/→ at 1440 and 1000 px. Median ▸ Radius 'abc', '2,5,1', '2,,5', '0,25', '7' by click and by Enter. New Image 20 frames → Z Project, verified against numpy. Synthetic nuclei → Analyze Particles → 'Auto-threshold and run' → ROI Manager Clear…/Undo clear → Results Clear…/Undo clear → preview + IJM. Save As of the projection → Gaussian '1,5' → ⌘S → tag dump, plus a control with a file opened from disk (Open → Invert → Save As → Smooth → ⌘S). Tracks wizard detect 60 → step 2 → Back → 84 → 70 → step 2. Help ▸ Design & Research Notes / Command Reference / README. Regression pass: Image ▸ Adjust, Process ▸ Filters, Plugins ▸ Batch, Analyze ▸ Tools and Image ▸ Lookup Tables submenus (hit-tests); palette 'fire', 'bleach', 'open sample', 'gausian blur', 'thresold' and Enter on 'fire'; Gaussian sheet with Preview → Cancel; recorder lines (lumen.select targeting, lumen.display, → IJM in the UI); Image ▸ Adjust ▸ Threshold… → Analyze Particles; rectangle + M on blobs; a fresh 'Blobs' and 'Blobs (25K)' with a whole-image Measure; the Apply Recorded Macro to Folder sheet; closing a modified image by its tab ×. Not covered: screen reader, several users, a real folder batch run. Clean-up: File ▸ Close All (7 images, 'Close without saving'); ROI Manager (80) and Results (83) cleared through their confirmed dialogs; the 'Particle Summary' table removed with lumen.session.tables.clear(); my recorder cleared with its Clear button (count 0); a probe recorder I had created with curl ('e11probe', empty) deleted. My two Open Recent entries (blobs.gif, saved_max_ts_e11.tif) were removed from lumen.session.recent and ~/.lumen/recent.json; the other 18 entries are untouched, and a backup of the original file is in the e11tools scratch folder. Final /api/state: 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 Results rows, recorder 0 lines, 0 tables. No Chrome/Playwright process of mine is left. Kept as evidence next to this file: screenshots, recorder_preview.json, recorder_ijm.txt, tiff_tags.txt, saved_max_ts_e11.tif, opened_then_saved_e11b.tif.

reassessment.evidence: At 1440×900 and 1000×800: F10 focuses BUTTON 'File' (role menuitem). ↓ opens the menu and moves focus into it (DIV menuitem 'Open… ⌘O', highlighted). More ↓ goes to 'Open Recent', then 'Open Sample'. Home goes back to 'Open…', End to 'Text'. → opens the Text submenu with focus on 'Append Text…', ↓ goes to 'Set Text…', ← goes back to 'Text'. Esc returns focus to the 'File' trigger. F10 then ← wraps to 'Help', and ↓ focuses 'Keyboard Shortcuts'. Enter opened the 'Keyboard shortcuts' dialog with focus inside it (role=dialog). Mouse-opened File: ↓ goes to 'Open…', then → on a top-level item switches to the Edit menu with focus on its first enabled item ('Repeat Last Command'; Undo is disabled with nothing open), ↓ goes to 'Copy to System', ← goes back to File with focus on 'Open…'. Esc goes back to the 'File' trigger, a second Esc closes everything. Focus never fell to <body>. Screenshots 01_kbd_f10_down.png, 02_kbd_down3.png, 03_kbd_enter_item.png, 04_mouse_then_arrows.png, 05_kbd_1000_down.png.
reassessment.comment: Keyboard menus now behave like a normal desktop menubar at both widths. Keyboard-only users have the menus back.

reassessment.evidence: Help ▸ Design & Research Notes is still in the Help menu (between 'Fiji Parity' and 'ImageJ Website ↗'). It opens the docs dialog with five buttons 'README | Commands | Fiji parity | Design | Research' on the 'Design' page: 'Lumen — design notes … What the research says / Fiji's documented UX problems / More than 1,100 commands live in deeply nested dropdown menus (JoVE 2026, EasyFiji method article) … "Window soup" … Dialogs are modal and blind: most filters have no live preview, and the ones that do (Gaussian, Median...) hide it behind a checkbox … Only one undo level.' 'Research' opens 'Scientific image-analysis GUIs: a sourced review for Lumen … Lumen re-implements the Fiji/ImageJ toolbox behind a single-window, keyboard-first UI (DESIGN.md). This document is the evidence base for that design …'. Help ▸ Command Reference and Help ▸ Lumen README open the same five-button dialog. The tab buttons still have no role=tab/aria-selected (0 [role=tab], 0 [role=tablist] in the dialog). The Markdown is rendered badly: every wrapped bullet breaks into a bullet line plus a separate paragraph ('… (JoVE 2026, EasyFiji' / 'method article). Users …'). Emphasis shows as literal asterisks ('*napari*:', '*QuPath*:', '*Compiled November 2026 …*'). A 'Filter table rows…' search box sits above the prose and takes the initial focus. Screenshots 60_design_research_notes.png, 61_notes_research.png, 61_notes_design.png, 62_command_reference.png.
reassessment.comment: My judgement: if it was kept on purpose, I can see why. A short 'why Lumen looks the way it does' page helps Fiji users understand the single-window design, and the Research review with sources is honest. But as shipped, this is the developers' internal design brief, not user help. It opens with a list of Fiji's failings, cites 'DESIGN.md', and some sentences are now wrong about Lumen's own sheets: Median here hides Preview behind a checkbox exactly as described. The rendering is broken (split bullets, raw asterisks), and it shares the Help dialog's tab strip so it's one click from the Command reference. In a facility I'd rather it weren't on the first menu people open for help. Move it under Help ▸ About Lumen ▸ Design background (or link it from README), render the Markdown properly and give the tab strip tab semantics. It costs no work and loses no data, so severity stays 1.

reassessment.evidence: Median ▸ Radius on Blobs. 'abc', '2,5,1' and '2,,5' now each give aria-invalid=true, an inline message 'Radius is not a number', and a disabled Apply (disabled=true, title 'Radius: type a number first'). Clicking Apply does nothing (recorder count unchanged, sheet stays open). But Enter in the field still runs the command: with 'abc' in the field (value read just before the key press, Apply disabled, focus in the Radius spinbutton) Enter closed the sheet and the recorder gained lumen.run("filters.median", radius=2.0, shape='disk', scope='slice'), the default, not what the field showed. No toast. '2,5,1' + Enter and '2,,5' + Enter did the same. For comparison, the out-of-range '0,25' + Enter is blocked (sheet stays open, nothing recorded), and a valid '7' + Enter runs radius=7.0. Screenshots 10_median_abc.png, 11_median_251.png, 12_median_2comma5.png, 13_median_abc_before_enter.png, 14_median_abc_after_enter.png.
reassessment.comment: Half there. Clicking is protected now, but Enter isn't, and Enter is how I confirm every dialog in Fiji. The original consequence (a slipped key silently runs the default radius) still happens on the keyboard path. The range check already blocks Enter, so the non-numeric check should do the same.

reassessment.evidence: Z Project of 'timeseries_e11' → File ▸ Save As… eval_e11/saved_max_ts_e11.tif → Gaussian σ '1,5' → ⌘S (toast 'Saved …/saved_max_ts_e11.tif'). TIFF dump (tifffile from the project .venv): Software 'Lumen 0.1.0'; ImageDescription 'ImageJ=1.54p images=1 hyperstack=true mode=color unit=pixel spacing=1.0 finterval=0.0 min=0.0 max=255.0'. The ImageJ Info property reads: 'Lumen processing: Lumen 0.1.0, written 2026-11-13 14:43:37 / Derived from: timeseries_e11 ▸ Z Project (method='Max Intensity', start=1, stop=20, axis='Z') / Source: …/eval_e11/saved_max_ts_e11.tif / 1. Gaussian Blur (sigma=1.5, scaled_units=False)'. So the derivation line now carries its parameters, but 'Source:' still names the file itself. Control with a real opened file: File ▸ Open… saved_max_ts_e11.tif → Invert → Save As opened_then_saved_e11b.tif → Smooth → ⌘S. Its Info keeps the earlier block and appends 'Lumen 0.1.0, written 2026-11-13 14:44:20 / Source: …/eval_e11/saved_max_ts_e11.tif / 1. Invert / 2. Smooth'. Here Source is the opened file, which is correct, and the chain is preserved. tiff_tags.txt; files saved_max_ts_e11.tif and opened_then_saved_e11b.tif (kept next to this file as evidence).
reassessment.comment: Two out of three now. Derived-from parameters: fixed. Source for an opened file: correct, and the history chains across files nicely. But for an image that was never opened from disk (a projection of a New Image), 'Source:' still points at the file being written, so the log says the file is derived from itself. That self-reference is then carried into every descendant's Info. The line should be left out, or say 'Source: (unsaved) timeseries_e11'. Also, the derived_from line says axis='Z' although frames were projected (see E10-6).

reassessment.evidence: Tracks ▸ Wizard on 'timeseries_e11' (20 noise frames, radius 2.5). Detect at quality 60 gives '94 spots in 20 frames (quality ≥ 60)'. Next shows step 2 with the slider at 60.04 (range input 60.0417…, text '60.042') and 'Quality ≥ 60.04: keeps ≈ 94 of 94 spots (detected spots; median 62.55)'. Back, detect at 84: on this random series that gives '0 spots in 0 frames (quality ≥ 84) – lower the quality threshold or the radius, then detect again'. Next is then disabled ('Detect spots first (a run with 0 spots does not count)'), so a stale step 2 can't be reached. Detect again at 70 gives '6 spots in 6 frames (quality ≥ 70)'. Next shows step 2 re-seeded to 70.13 (range 70.1275…, text '70.128'), 'keeps ≈ 6 of 6 spots (median 71.34)', histogram 70.13–76.96. /api/state ROI count stayed at 41 (no spots dumped into the manager). Screenshots 50_tracks_wizard.png, 51_tracks_step2_q60.png, 52_tracks_step1_q84.png, 53_tracks_step2_q70.png.
reassessment.comment: Step 2 now follows the latest detection, and a zero-spot run can't be carried into it. My series has a different random seed than E10's, so 84 gave 0 spots instead of 1; 70 was the equivalent check.

reassessment.comment: It now behaves like Fiji: a single-slice time-lapse is projected over its frames on the first try. Cosmetic leftovers: the sheet still says 'Collapse the Z axis' and 'Stop … 0 = last slice' for what is really a frame range. The recorder and the image's derived_from metadata write axis='Z' although frames were projected. That replays correctly in Lumen, but the provenance line names the wrong axis.

The recorder has rois.clear, rois.restore_cleared, analyze.clear_results, results.restore_cleared. reassessment.comment: A clear I took back no longer replays in a batch or in the macro, and the script says why. The IJM line after auto-thresholding honestly tells the Fiji user to add setAutoThreshold. Better still would be to write the actual setAutoThreshold("Default dark") line.

regressions.location: File ▸ Open Sample ▸ Blobs (25K) (ImageJ's blobs.gif, downloaded from imagej.net)
regressions.observation: ImageJ's classic Blobs sample opens as a 3-channel RGB image with the GIF's inverting palette baked into the pixel values, instead of 8-bit with an inverting LUT as in ImageJ. Toast: 'Blobs (25K): 256×254, 1 slice(s), 3 channel(s), RGB'; Image Info 'Type RGB, 3 ch'. A whole-image Measure gives Mean 151.73, Min 7, Max 247. The GIF's raw index values (what ImageJ measures) have mean 103.27. 151.73 is exactly the mean after mapping through the inverted palette (255 − 103.27). Every Fiji tutorial (Measure, threshold, Analyze Particles on Blobs) will give different numbers in Lumen. The bundled 'Blobs' item is a different image (scikit-image blobs, 256×256, 8-bit, mean 84.54) with the same name. I can't tell from E10's report whether this is new, but E10 didn't mention it.
regressions.evidence: 80_blobs25k_fresh.png, 79_blobs_fresh.png; Results rows ['blobs.gif-1', 65024.0, 151.73, 7.0, 247.0] and ['blobs.tif', 65536.0, 84.54, 5.0, 252.0]; PIL on ~/.lumen/samples/blobs.gif: mode P, index mean 103.2686, palette[0]=(255,255,255), palette[255]=(0,0,0).

regressions.location: Plugins ▸ Batch ▸ Apply Recorded Macro to Folder… default 'Commands to run' list and GET /api/recorder/preview
regressions.observation: The sheet says the default list is 'the recorder's lines minus the open / save / close / select / display / undo ones'. It does drop file.sample, file.new and lumen.select. But the first default line is lumen.run("file.open_imagej_sample", name='Blobs (25K)', use_cache=True), which opens a sample. Run on a folder, every file would also open Blobs, and the following commands would act on Blobs rather than on the folder's file. Nothing in the summary flags the line ('26 recorded lines … will run on every file (17 open / save / select / display / undo lines left out …)').
regressions.evidence: 81_batch_sheet.png (textarea starts with the open_imagej_sample line); recorder_preview.json: that line is in 'lines' and 'script', while file.new and file.sample are in 'skipped'.

positives: Keyboard menus are fixed properly: F10, arrows, Home/End, Enter, Esc and submenu ←/→ all move real focus at 1440 and 1000 px, and ←/→ from a mouse-opened menu keeps focus in the menus.

Clear/restore pairs are now cancelled like undo pairs: neither the batch list nor the IJM export replays a clear I took back, and both say so ('Undone and left out: rois.clear, analyze.clear_results').
Z Project on a single-slice time-lapse now projects the frames on the first try (numerically identical to a numpy max over t).
Tracks step 2 re-seeds its threshold after every detection, and a zero-spot detection can't be carried forward.
Non-numeric sheet input now gets an inline message ('Radius is not a number') and a disabled Apply with an explanatory tooltip.
The provenance log in the ImageJ Info property now carries the derivation parameters and chains across files: a re-opened file keeps its earlier log and adds a new block with the correct Source.

The regression pass found the earlier fixes intact. All submenus I opened are fully hit-testable, palette fuzzy search copes with 'gausian blur', 'bleach' finds Bleach Correction, 'fire' applies the LUT and records it, and Gaussian Preview → Cancel restores the image without a History or recorder entry. The recorder writes lumen.select/lumen.display lines that → IJM turns into selectWindow/setMinAndMax. Analyze Particles on a thresholded image records auto_threshold=False with size 20–∞, and the modified-image close dialog defaults focus to Cancel and offers Save….
overall: Round 4 fixed most of what I flagged. Of my seven items, four are fixed (E10-1 keyboard menus, E10-5 Tracks re-seeding, E10-6 Z Project over frames, and the clear/restore half of E7-5), two are partly fixed (E10-3, E10-4) and one is unchanged (E10-2, which looks deliberate). On a single-user facility workstation I'd now hand Lumen to Fiji users, with three warnings. First, pressing Enter in a sheet with a non-numeric value still silently runs the default (abc + Enter → Median radius 2.0). Clicking Apply is blocked, but Enter isn't. Second, the folder batch's default list keeps a 'open ImageJ sample' line, so read the list before Apply. Third, ImageJ's Blobs sample opens as RGB with the inverted palette baked in, so Measure gives 151.7 instead of ImageJ's 103.3. That's exactly the kind of tutorial mismatch that makes facility users distrust a tool. Provenance is close: the derivation now has parameters, but an image never opened from disk still names itself as its Source. Design & Research Notes is harmless but should move out of the main Help path and be rendered properly. What still blocks a shared facility server is unchanged from E10 (E7-21, not re-tested in depth): one shared Open Recent list (I had to remove my own entries by hand), shared ROI Manager/Results/tables, the server's file system and unrestricted Python as the server account.
